question: Rapidly adapting receptors?
explanation: Free nerve endings (Nonencapsulated Receptors): Location - Epidermis, cornea, gut, dermis, ligaments, joint capsules, bone, dental pulp, etc. Hairless skin, Hairy skin. Stimulus - Mechanoreceptor. Sensory Modality - Pain (fast), pain (slow), touch (crude), Pressure, heat and cold. Adaptability - Rapid. Fibers - A delta, C. Meissner's corpuscles (Encapsulated Receptors): Location - Dermal papillae of skin of palm and sole of foot. Stimulus - Mechanoreceptor. Sensory Modality - Touch. Adaptability - Rapid. Fibers - A beta. Pacinian Corpuscles (Encapsulated Receptors): Location - Dermis, ligaments, joint capsules, peritoneum, external genitalia, etc. Stimulus - Mechanoreceptor. Sensory Modality - Vibration. Adaptability - Rapid. Fibers - A beta. Ruffini's Corpuscles (Encapsulated Receptors): Location - Dermis of hairy skin. Stimulus - Mechanoreceptor. Sensory Modality - Stretch. Adaptability - Slow. Fibers - A beta.

question: When cold water is placed in the external ear during the caloric test, the cellular mechanism in the horizontal semicircular canal hair cells that leads to nystagmus is:

options.A: Depolarization of hair cells -> increased vestibular nerve firing
options.B: Hyperpolarization of hair cells -> decreased vestibular nerve firing
options.C: Release of endolymph -> increased cupula rigidity
options.D: Hyperpolarization of hair cells -> increased vestibular nerve firing

explanation: Cold water cools the horizontal semicircular canal -> endolymph sinks -> deflects cupula away from kinocilium. This hyperpolarizes hair cells, reducing the firing rate of the vestibular nerve on that side. The asymmetry between left and right vestibular firing triggers the vestibulo-ocular reflex, causing slow eye movement toward the irrigated ear and fast nystagmus away.
